Title: “Injuries Among Maryland Jockeys During Thoroughbred Racing: 2015-2019”
Subtitle: Source 3
Author: Kelly Ryan, et al.
Content: ...Thoroughbred horse racing is `text(one)` of the most competitive and popular sports
worldwide, but it is very physically demanding and not without substantial risk. Jockeys are
elite athletes who sit perched atop an animal weighing `10` times their mass while galloping
at speeds up to `text(64 km/h)` (`text(40 mph)`). A `text(single)` misstep or slight error may result in the jockey
being thrown from the horse, potentially resulting in catastrophic injury or death. While
most reported injuries have been associated with falls, there are also injuries that can result
from training activities or simply being in close proximity to a horse. ...
The Maryland Jockey Club is the oldest professional sports organisation in the USA.
In `2015`, it developed the Horsemen's Health Program, which implemented primary care
sports medicine physicians to provide medical coverage at the racetracks across the state.
Maryland racetracks operate `text(year-round)`, with approximately `160` racing `text(days per year)`,
averaging `200` riders `text(annually)`, usually between `20-35` jockeys riding `text(per day)`, throughout the
state. Maryland only races `text(one)` track in the state at any given time. ...

References: incidents — any events involving a jockey requiring an evaluation by the racetrack physician and resulting in an injury report
injuries — any physical complaints sustained by any person resulting from interaction with racehorses or related activities
falls — riders being dislodged from a horse, regardless of outcome
horse breakdown — when a horse can no longer bear its body weight
clipped heels — when a horse steps on the heels of the horse in front of it
impact with horse — of the `11` instances of 'Impact With Horse,' `text(six)` of those injuries were caused by being headbutted by a horse
pulling up — when a jockey brings a horse to a stop during a race
